summary: This note is the reference page for the Snowflake SQL command DROP DATABASE, which removes a database from the system. It covers the command syntax, the name and CASCADE/RESTRICT parameters, Time Travel and Fail-safe behavior after a drop, restoration by renaming, notes on database replication (secondary and primary databases), and two usage examples showing the status output and SHOW DATABASES HISTORY results.
one_line: Reference for the Snowflake DROP DATABASE command, covering CASCADE/RESTRICT, Time Travel and Fail-safe recovery, and replication restrictions.
key_facts: DROP DATABASE syntax is: DROP DATABASE [ IF EXISTS ] <name> [ CASCADE | RESTRICT ].
The default for the CASCADE | RESTRICT option is CASCADE.
CASCADE drops the database and all objects in it, including tables with primary/unique keys referenced by foreign keys in other tables.
RESTRICT returns a warning about existing foreign key references and does not drop the database.
Identifiers containing spaces, special characters, or mixed-case characters must be enclosed in double quotes, and such quoted identifiers are case-sensitive.
Within the Time Travel retention period, a dropped database can be restored.
In Fail-safe (7 days), a dropped database can be recovered, but only by Snowflake.
A transient database has no Fail-safe, so it is purged when it moves out of Time Travel.
Once a dropped database has been purged, it cannot be recovered and must be recreated.

When a database is dropped, data retention periods explicitly set on child schemas or tables differ from the database are not honored; child objects are retained for the database's period, so they should be dropped explicitly first.
After dropping a database, creating a database with the same name creates a new version; the dropped version can be restored by renaming the current version to a different name.
The DROP operation fails if a session policy or password policy is set on a user or the account.
Only the database owner (the role with the OWNERSHIP privilege on the database) can drop the database.
A primary database cannot be dropped while one or more replicas (secondary databases) exist.
To drop a primary database with replicas, promote a secondary database to primary and then drop the former primary, or drop all its secondary databases first.
In the example, DROP DATABASE mytestdb2 returned the status 'MYTESTDB2 successfully dropped.'
